rows.text: The season results stage is lit like a shop window, and {winner} steps into the glare alone.
{loser} reads the season sheet like a jeweller hunting for a scratch on the glass.
Every shelf on the results stage has been dusted, and {winner} is already waiting at the glass.
Engraved name plates line the back wall, and {loserClub} waits quietly for its name to be read.
Keys in hand, {winner} and the results board share a long, hushed moment before the figures go up.
Ribbons drape the lectern, silver sits on the sideboard, and {winnerClub} is polished for the night.
The results board glows at the far end of the stage while {loser} checks the cabinet glass once more.
A velvet-lined case waits by the results desk, empty for now, as {managerA} and {managerB} reach for the shelves.
Medals are laid out in a row across the stage, and the final figures are still hidden under a cloth.
The stage is set, every case lit, and {winnerClub} keeps its silver in the middle of the room.
Nobody needs an engraving tool tonight, only a steady hand on the results sheet and a cabinet about to fill.
{loserClub} sits beside a shelf of silver that looks heavier than it did before the reading began.
Before the season is read out, {winner} gives the trophy cabinet a final polish, more ritual than need.
The results stage is where the year's silverware gets counted, and {loser} arrives with a cloth and a steady gaze.
Lights rise over a row of glass cases and a sealed ledger, the season locked inside, waiting for the reading.
Keys jangle at the back of the hall as {managerA} unlocks the results room with {managerB} close behind.
That season's results sit on the lectern like the last piece on a shelf, and nobody has touched the glass yet.
Matching display cases stand side by side, and {managerA} and {managerB} look at them with the same level gaze.
The scales in the trophy room sit perfectly still, weighed down by equal silver on either side for {clubA} and {clubB}.
A matched pair of keys hangs on the same hook, and neither {managerA} nor {managerB} is ready to reach for it.
{clubA} and {clubB} have shelves that match in polish and shine, a stalemate of silver nobody wants to break.
Engraved plates sit in a neat line, and the names of {managerA} and {managerB} are cut at exactly the same depth.
The medals stop swinging together, and {managerA} and {managerB} exchange a nod across the glass.
A ribbon for {clubA}, a ribbon for {clubB}, both tied in the same knot and both waiting for a verdict.
{managerA} wipes the glass, {managerB} wipes the glass, and the reflections look like twins.
Dust settles evenly across both display cases, and neither {managerA} nor {managerB} has found a reason to claim the top shelf.
The ledger closes with the bottom line inked the same on both pages, {clubA} and {clubB} alike.
A stand-off in silver: {clubA} and {clubB} with cabinets of equal weight and polish, glowing in the spotlight.
The velvet is pressed flat on both shelves, marking the spot where a trophy would sit if the scoreboard tilted.
{managerB} hands over the cloth, {managerA} hands it straight back, and the cabinet keeps its shine a little longer.
Keys turn in the same lock at the same moment, and {managerA} and {managerB} stare at the gap between the cases.
Silver goes back on the shelves in matching pairs for {clubA} and {clubB}, the room hushed and perfectly balanced.
Matched sets of engraved trophies lean towards each other on the sideboard, and {managerA} and {managerB} watch them like equal rivals.
Under the spotlight the medals sit in a neat, even row, and {managerA} and {managerB} hold their breath together.
The final stage is lit for a lone winner, and {winner} walks towards the cabinet with the keys already in hand.
Curtains part on the last shelf, and {winnerClub} is the name being engraved onto the newest plate.
{winner} is handed the last key to the trophy room while {loser} watches from the far end of the hall.
The final results are read aloud, and {winner} lifts the plate as if it had been waiting there all along.
A spotlight, a silver case and a name not yet engraved: {winnerClub} steps up to claim the last piece.
Every glass door in the hall swings open at once, and {winner} steps into the brightest light the cabinet can give.
{loserClub} still has a cloth in hand, but the final case belongs to {winnerClub} now, and the hall applauds.
The last medal goes onto the velvet, the engraving is done, and {winner} stands before the cabinet with nothing else to polish.
Stage lights find {winner} alone at the lectern, the final sheet in hand and silver shining behind.
The curtain call is slow, the case is open, and {winner} lifts the trophy as if the room had been waiting.
{loser} offers a handshake across the open cabinet, and {winner} accepts it with the final plaque tucked under an arm.
A last ribbon is tied to the top shelf, and {winnerClub} has the only knot in the room that matters.
Rolls of silver paper, a locked case and a blank plaque: {winner} is about to write the closing line.
Quiet now, the cabinet full, and {winner} takes the closing bow beside the glass.
Every key in the room has turned, every shelf is checked, and {winnerClub} has the last case to fill.
A last polish on the trophy, a glance at the cabinet, and {winner} steps into frame as the season's closing picture.
The finale on the results board is simple: {winner} with the last key, {loser} at the back, the cabinet open.
Every shelf in the trophy room is gilded tonight, and {winner} walks the aisle as if the gold were a gift.
Gold leaf catches the light on every cabinet, and {winnerClub} stands in the glow with a cloth in hand.
The room has turned to gold, and {loser} studies the gleaming shelves with a grin.
Engraved gold plates line the wall, and {managerA} and {managerB} gaze back at their reflections like rival kings.
Under the golden lamps, the medals shine so brightly that {winnerClub} has to squint to read the plaques.
Gold trim runs along each display case, and {winner} wipes a fingerprint off the glass before anyone notices.
Every key on the golden ring has been polished, and {winner} turns the largest slowly in the lock.
The gilded cabinet is open, the velvet glows, and {loser} steps back to let the light fall on the silver.
A room of gold, a row of ribbons and a manager at ease: {winner}, centre of it all.
Gold paint on the old wood, gold ink on the new plate, and {winnerClub} sets the latest trophy on the middle shelf.
The trophy room is warm with gold, and {managerA} runs a finger along the cool glass beside {managerB}.
Gilt frames hang over the cabinets, and {winner} checks each engraving with the patience of a collector.
Golden light spills across the silver, catching every medal and the faces of {managerA} and {managerB} alike.
Copper and gold cover the shelves, and {loserClub} holds its silver a little closer to the chest.
Gold covers the cabinet and the ribbons, and {winner} stands before it looking like a manager who has earned the lights.
Each golden shelf holds a little more silver than before, and {winnerClub} keeps the brightest piece at eye level.
The gold room is quiet and {loser} lifts a trophy only to set it down again, admiring the shine.
{winner} raises both arms beside the cabinet, a medal swinging from a hand.
Arms wide and a grin wider still, {winner} celebrates in front of the silver as though the shelves had cheered.
{winner} punches the air with a ribbon in a fist, the trophy case glowing behind a very happy manager.
The cabinet door is open and {winner} is already dancing, careful not to bump the polished silver.
{winnerClub} wears the kit proudly as {winner} lifts the nearest trophy and holds it up like a prize at a village fair.
{winner} hugs a gleaming cup as if it might try to escape the glass.
{winner} cheers at the mirror-bright cabinet, a hand on the shelf and the other on a golden plaque.
A ring of keys jingles as {winner} jumps, the celebration rattling the whole trophy room.
Silver held high, a broad smile, and {winner} shows the shelf that the year's good work has come home.
{winner} takes a bow mid-room, a ribbon draped over an arm and eyes fixed on the newest case.
There is no quiet moment for {winnerClub}: {winner} spins round with a medal and a shout that rattles the glass.
The plaques rattle as {winner} thumps the cabinet with delight, and the trophy room has never looked so happy.
{winner} lifts a silver cup above the head, joy written across the face of the manager in the Showdown kit.
A victory lap around the trophy shelves, cloth over the shoulder, and {winner} is the happiest soul in the room.
{winner} holds the cup close and sways a little, the sort of celebration that needs a whole shelf to contain it.
With the cabinet unlocked and the medals ready, {winner} celebrates like a manager who has waited a long time for this room.
{loser} sits before the empty case, chin in a hand, working out where the next trophy will come from.
Deep in thought, {loser} studies the silver as if it were a puzzle still missing a key.
{loserClub} keeps a tight grip on a cloth while {loser} stares at the shelf and tries to remember what worked.
Late night, quiet room, and {loser} sits by the cabinet, already thinking about the next save file.
A stool, a cold cup and a manager who is really thinking: {loser} watches a lone medal turn slowly under the lamp.
{managerA} rests a thumb on the ledger, lost in the sums, while the trophy room waits in silence.
{loser} traces a crack in the display glass with a finger, serious as a historian reading an old plaque.
Head bowed and eyes on the plaques, {loser} plans the season ahead shelf by shelf.
{winner} sits on the velvet bench with a faraway look, weighing the silver against the years still to come.
The controller rests on {loser}'s knee as the screen dims, and the next save file is already forming in the manager's head.
Under a night sky of hanging lamps, {loserClub} sits lost in thought beside a shelf of engraved names.
{managerB} leans back with arms folded, deep in thought about what the next season might bring to the dusty shelves.
{loser} stares past the glass into the reflection, as if the answer were engraved somewhere behind it.
Like a chess player after a long night, {loser} sits still by the cabinet, weighing each piece of silver in turn.
{clubA} keeps its silver under a lamp, and {managerA} rubs the back of the neck, deep in thought over the next move.
Pressing pause on the year, {loser} sits quietly among the trophies, weighing the ribbons and the lessons of the table.
